title: Prabhas Raised Three Fingers. Rana Tried to Stop Him. The Internet Did the Math.
excerpt: Netflix's 'Baahubali: The Torchbearer' was supposed to be a nostalgic four-part documentary celebrating ten years of Mahishmati. Then a ten-second clip in the finale became the most discussed moment in Indian cinema this week.
body:
Somewhere around the forty-minute mark of the final episode of *Baahubali: The Torchbearer*, something happens that has nothing to do with nostalgia and everything to do with the future.

Rana Daggubati is sitting across from the camera, loose-limbed and grinning, when he says it almost casually: "The world may not be ready yet, but there will be Baahubali..." Before he can finish, Prabhas — sitting next to him — slowly, deliberately raises three fingers. Anushka Shetty bursts out laughing. Rana lunges to pull his hand down. The screen cuts to black. A single line appears: *And the legacy continues.*

The internet hasn't slept since.

Ten Years of Mahishmati, in Four Hours

Let's rewind. *Baahubali: The Torchbearer* dropped on Netflix on June 26, streaming in Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, and Malayalam — timed to the tenth anniversary of the franchise that rewired Indian cinema's ambitions. It's a four-part docuseries, each episode under forty minutes, produced by Arka Mediaworks and built around the people who made the duology happen.

And what a roster. SS Rajamouli anchors the narrative, walking viewers through the years when Mahishmati existed only in his head and on a few napkin sketches. Prabhas, Rana, Anushka Shetty, Ramya Krishnan, Tamannaah Bhatia, Sathyaraj, and Nassar all appear, not in character but as themselves — older, more reflective, and clearly still a little stunned by what they built together.

> "Sathyaraj, the veteran who played Kattappa, reflects on how the "Why did Kattappa kill Baahubali?" phenomenon became bigger than any film he'd ever done in a career spanning four decades."

Producer Shobu Yarlagadda described the project to Gulte as "a tribute to the film's ten-year journey, its creative process, and its influence on popular culture." Netflix's official logline is more blunt: *From production setbacks to financial crises, the Baahubali cast and crew recount the demanding journey behind the beloved epic film series.*

The Stories They Never Told

![The Torchbearer — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/b/be/Svetlonosfilm.jpg)

The first two episodes cover familiar ground — how Rajamouli pitched an epic that no one believed could be made in Telugu cinema, how the budget ballooned, how Prabhas committed nearly five years of his career to the role. But the docuseries earns its keep in the details that never made it to press junkets.

There's the financial crisis that nearly shut down production mid-shoot. The VFX battles where entire sequences were rebuilt from scratch because Rajamouli kept pushing for one more iteration. The construction of the Mahishmati kingdom set — the sheer physical ambition of building a world before CGI could fill in the gaps. Costume design, action choreography, and the political dynamics of making a Pan-India film before Pan-India was even a term the industry used.

The third episode is the emotional core. Prabhas talks about what it cost him to vanish from the public eye for half a decade. Anushka Shetty gets candid about the physical toll of playing Devasena. Sathyaraj, the veteran who played Kattappa, reflects on how the "Why did Kattappa kill Baahubali?" phenomenon became bigger than any film he'd ever done in a career spanning four decades.

So, Is Baahubali 3 Happening?

Nobody has said yes on record. But nobody has said no with a straight face, either.

The three-finger moment is deliberate. This isn't a blooper or an unguarded aside — it's in a produced, edited docuseries released by Netflix. If the filmmakers wanted to kill the speculation, they would have cut the clip. Instead, they made it the closer.

The practical reality: Rajamouli is neck-deep in *Varanasi*, his next directorial starring Mahesh Babu, Priyanka Chopra, and Prithviraj Sukumaran, slated for April 2027. Prabhas has his own stack of commitments. A Baahubali 3 is, at best, a 2029 conversation.

But the legacy of the franchise is undeniable. *Baahubali: The Beginning* (2015) was India's highest-grossing Telugu film of its year. *Baahubali 2: The Conclusion* (2017) shattered every record in sight and turned Prabhas into a genuine Pan-India phenomenon. The remastered combined cut, *Baahubali: The Epic*, landed in theatres as recently as October 2025. The franchise doesn't just endure — it compounds.

Where to Watch

For the diaspora, this is effortless. *Baahubali: The Torchbearer* is streaming now on Netflix worldwide in Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, and Malayalam. Four episodes, each under forty minutes. You can finish it in a single evening — and then spend the rest of the night arguing about whether Prabhas really just confirmed the biggest sequel in Indian cinema history.

Our take? He did. And Rana knows it.
